points.description: Correct identification of the power calculation method (P = VI) using the 6V source and 10mA current.
Correct application of the energy-time relationship (t = E/P) to determine the operating time.
Correct numerical computation, including proper unit conversions (e.g., mA to A, W to mW).
Final answer stated clearly with appropriate units (e.g., seconds or hours).

rubric.notes: Full marks are awarded for a correct derivation of power followed by the correct calculation of time. Part marks are awarded for correct methodology even if arithmetic errors occur. No marks are awarded if the student fails to identify the relationship between energy, power, and time.
rubric.answer_key: Assuming a standard energy capacity for 4 AA cells (e.g., 6 Wh or 21600 J). P = 6V * 0.01A = 0.06W. t = E/P. If E = 2160 J, t = 36000 s.
